name: Romans
subtitle: A Case Made of Scripture
howToRead: Romans is an argument conducted in citations. Paul reasons by quoting — “as it is written,” “the scripture says,” “Isaiah cries out” — and at the turning points the proof is a chain of texts laid end to end: the indictment of all humanity in chapter 3, the midrash on Abraham’s faith in chapter 4, and above all the dense scriptural catena of chapters 9–11, where the destiny of Israel is argued almost entirely in the words of the Law and the Prophets. The chips beside each passage name the Scripture underneath it — solid for a formal quotation, dashed for an allusion, dotted for a fainter echo, ◇ for a figural pattern that borrows no words. A lighter chip and a trailing ? mark an echo that is faint or contested. Where Paul follows the Greek of the Septuagint against the Hebrew, both readings are shown.

pericopes.text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart for the Good News of God, which he promised before through his prophets in the holy Scriptures, concerning his Son, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh, who was declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord, through whom we received grace and apostleship, for obedience of faith among all the nations, for his name’s sake; among whom you are also called to belong to Jesus Christ; to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

echoes.text: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
echoes.note: The gospel 'promised before' (v.2) and the apostolic 'set apart' echo the prophetic-promise schema; faint thematic link to the awaited word that surely comes. Low volume, no verbal borrowing here, but coheres with the Hab 2:4 citation in 1:17.
echoes.lxxText: For the vision is yet for a time, and it shall shoot forth at the end, and not in vain: though he should tarry, wait for him; for he will surely come, and will not tarry.

echoes.text: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news of good, who publishes salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
echoes.note: 'Good News of God' (euangelion) draws on the Isaianic herald who announces good tidings; Paul's gospel vocabulary recurrently leans on Isaiah's heralding of salvation. Thematic coherence high with Romans' Isaiah-saturated argument; volume moderate.

echoes.text: The Spirit of the Lord Yahweh is on me; because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to those who are bound;
echoes.note: Set-apart, Spirit-anointed proclamation of good news. Faint; supports the euangelizo background but little distinctive verbal contact.

echoes.text: When your days are fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your fathers, I will set up your seed after you, who shall proceed out of your bowels, and I will establish his kingdom. He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever. I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men;
echoes.note: 'Born of the seed of David' and 'declared Son of God' (vv.3-4) invoke the Nathan oracle: Davidic seed whom God will establish and call son. High thematic coherence (royal-messianic sonship) and strong conceptual recurrence in early Christian use.

echoes.text: I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
echoes.note: 'Declared to be the Son of God with power... by the resurrection' echoes the enthronement decree 'You are my Son'; standard messianic proof-text read of Christ's vindication. Strong thematic coherence with Davidic sonship; satisfaction high.

echoes.text: Yahweh says to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool for your feet.”
echoes.note: Resurrection-enthronement of 'our Lord' faintly invokes the royal session psalm pervasive in NT Christology. Low verbal volume here.

echoes.text: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit. The Spirit of Yahweh will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh. His delight will be in the fear of Yahweh. He will not judge by the sight of his eyes, neither decide by the hearing of his ears; but with righteousness he will judge the poor, and decide with equity for […]
echoes.note: Davidic shoot bringing the nations to obedience; 'obedience of faith among all the nations' coheres with the root-of-Jesse hope (cf. Rom 15:12 quoting Isa 11:10). Anticipatory, faint here.

pericopes.text: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, that your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world. For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Good News of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you always in my prayers, requesting, if by any means now at last I may be prospered by the will of God to come to you. For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, to the end that you may be established; that is, that I with you may be encouraged in you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine. Now I don’t desire to have you unaware, brothers, that I often planned to come to you, and was hindered so far, that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among the rest of the Gentiles. I am debtor both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to the wise and to the foolish. So, as much as is in me, I am eager to preach the Good News to you also who are in Rome.

For I am not ashamed of the Good News of Christ, for it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes; for the Jew first, and also for the Greek. For in it is revealed God’s righteousness from faith to faith. As it is written, “But the righteous shall live by faith.”

echoes.text: Behold, his soul is puffed up. It is not upright in him, but the righteous will live by his faith.
echoes.note: Formula-marked ('As it is written') verbatim citation: 'the righteous shall live by faith.' The thesis-text of Romans. Highest volume and satisfaction; Paul reads ho dikaios ek pisteos against the LXX/MT to ground righteousness-by-faith.

echoes.text: Yahweh has made known his salvation. He has openly shown his righteousness in the sight of the nations.
echoes.note: 'God's righteousness... revealed' echoes the psalmist's 'The LORD has made known his salvation; he has revealed his righteousness (dikaiosyne) in the sight of the nations.' Strong conceptual pairing of revealed righteousness + salvation to the nations; moderate volume.

echoes.text: “Attend to me, my people; and give ear to me, my nation: for a law shall go out from me, and I will establish my justice for a light of the peoples. My righteousness is near, my salvation has gone out, and my arms shall judge the peoples; the islands shall wait for me, and on my arm shall they trust. Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look on the earth beneath; for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment; […]
echoes.note: Isaiah's coupling of God's 'righteousness' and 'salvation' going forth to the peoples grounds Paul's revealed dikaiosyne theou unto salvation. Recurrent in Romans; thematic coherence high.

echoes.text: Therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh, “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation. He who believes shall not act hastily.
echoes.note: 'Everyone who believes' / not being put to shame anticipates Paul's later quotation of Isa 28:16 (Rom 9:33; 10:11); 'not ashamed' may already lean on this shame-vindication motif. Faint here, recurrence elsewhere.

echoes.text: I will also speak of your statutes before kings, and will not be disappointed.
echoes.note: 'I am not ashamed' to speak of God's testimonies before kings; possible background to 'not ashamed of the gospel.' Low volume, contested.

pericopes.text: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who suppress the truth in unrighteousness, because that which is known of God is revealed in them, for God revealed it to them. For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divinity; that they may be without excuse. Because, knowing God, they didn’t glorify him as God, neither gave thanks, but became vain in their reasoning, and their senseless heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, and traded the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, and four-footed animals, and creeping things.

echoes.text: Thus they exchanged their glory for an image of a bull that eats grass.
echoes.note: 'Traded the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image' closely reworks 'they exchanged their glory for the image of an ox that eats grass' (golden calf). High verbal volume on exchange-of-glory; the calf episode is the paradigm of idolatrous substitution.

echoes.text: Has a nation changed its gods, which really are no gods? But my people have changed their glory for that which does not profit.
echoes.note: 'My people have exchanged their glory for that which does not profit' — same exchange-of-glory idiom Paul deploys (allasso/doxa). Strong verbal and conceptual parallel; recurrence reinforces Ps 106:20.

echoes.text: For verily all men by nature were but vain who had no perception of God, And from the good things that are seen they gained not power to know him that is, Neither by giving heed to the works did they recognize the architect; But either fire, or wind, or swift air, Or circling stars, or raging water, or luminaries of heaven, They thought to be gods that rule the world. And if it was through delight in their beauty that they took them to be gods, Let them […]
echoes.note: Paul's natural theology — God's invisible power/divinity perceived through created things, leaving idolaters 'without excuse,' yet they failed to know the Maker — closely tracks Wisdom 13's argument that those who study creation are 'without excuse' for not finding its Artisan. High volume; Paul demonstrably leans on Wisdom here.

echoes.text: But miserable were they, and in dead things were their hopes, Who called them gods which are works of men’s hands, Gold and silver, wrought with careful are, and likenesses of animals, Or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand. Yes and if some woodcutter, having sawn down a tree that is easily moved, Skilfully strippeth away all its bark, And fashioning it in comely form makes a vessel useful for the service of life; And burning the refuse of his […]
echoes.note: The catalogue of images (corruptible man, birds, beasts, creeping things) parallels Wisdom's mockery of those who fashion likenesses of corruptible things. Strong lexical/conceptual overlap; satisfaction high.

echoes.text: God said, “Let the waters abound with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of sky.” God created the large sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed, after their kind, and every winged bird after its kind. God saw that it was good. God blessed them, saying, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.” There was evening and there […]
echoes.note: The taxonomy 'man... birds... four-footed animals... creeping things' inverts the Genesis creation order; idolatry as anti-creation, worshipping the made over the Maker. Moderate verbal echo of the creature-categories; thematic coherence high.

echoes.text: Be very careful, for you saw no kind of form on the day that Yahweh spoke to you in Horeb out of the midst of the fire, lest you corrupt yourselves, and make yourself an engraved image in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female, the likeness of any animal that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the sky, the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the water under the […]
echoes.note: Moses' aniconic warning lists the very classes of image (likeness of male/female, beast, bird, creeping thing, heavenly bodies) Paul echoes; the LXX vocabulary of 'homoioma' overlaps. Strong verbal and conceptual support for the image-list.

echoes.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
echoes.note: 'Since the creation of the world' (apo ktiseos kosmou) and 'the things that are made' invoke the creation narrative as the ground of natural revelation. Moderate thematic coherence.

echoes.text: Everyone who makes an engraved image is vain. The things that they delight in will not profit. Their own witnesses don’t see, nor know, that they may be disappointed. Who has fashioned a god, or molds an image that is profitable for nothing? Behold, all his fellows will be disappointed; and the workmen are mere men. Let them all be gathered together. Let them stand up. They will fear. They will be put to shame together. The blacksmith takes an ax, works […]
echoes.note: Classic prophetic satire on idol-makers who become as senseless as their idols; 'became vain in their reasoning' and 'darkened heart' parallel Isaiah's blinded idolater. Moderate volume; recurrent idol-polemic.

echoes.text: The heavens declare the glory of God. The expanse shows his handiwork. Day after day they pour out speech, and night after night they display knowledge. There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard. Their voice has gone out through all the earth, their words to the end of the world. In them he has set a tent for the sun,
echoes.note: 'The heavens declare the glory of God' grounds Paul's claim that God's eternal power is 'clearly seen' through creation, leaving humanity without excuse. Thematic coherence high; moderate verbal contact.

echoes.text: “But ask the animals, now, and they shall teach you; the birds of the sky, and they shall tell you. Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach you. The fish of the sea shall declare to you. Who doesn’t know that in all these, the hand of Yahweh has done this,
echoes.note: Creation itself teaches the hand of God; supports natural revelation but faint verbal contact.

echoes.text: Every man has become brutish and without knowledge; every goldsmith is disappointed by his engraved image; for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.
echoes.note: 'Every man is become brutish in his knowledge' / idols are vanity — parallels 'became vain in their reasoning, professing wise they became fools.' Moderate recurrence within idol-polemic.

echoes.text: Yahweh knows the thoughts of man, that they are futile.
echoes.note: 'The LORD knows the thoughts of man, that they are vanity' faintly underlies 'became vain (emataiothesan) in their reasoning.' Low verbal volume.

echoes.text: Thus says Yahweh, “What unrighteousness have your fathers found in me, that they have gone far from me, and have walked after vanity, and are become vain?
echoes.note: 'They went after vanity and became vain' — same root for futility tied to idolatry; reinforces the exchange motif of Jer 2:11. Faint additional contact.

pericopes.text: Therefore God also gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to uncleanness, that their bodies should be dishonored among themselves, who exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen. For this reason, God gave them up to vile passions. For their women changed the natural function into that which is against nature. Likewise also the men, leaving the natural function of the woman, burned in their lust toward one another, men doing what is inappropriate with men, and receiving in themselves the due penalty of their error.

echoes.text: For the devising of idols was the beginning of fornication, And the invention of them the corruption of life: For neither were they from the beginning, neither will they be forever; For by the vaingloriousness of men they entered into the world, And therefore was a speedy end devised for them. For a father worn with untimely grief, Making an image of the child quickly taken away, Now honored him as a god which was then a dead man, And delivered to those […]
echoes.note: 'The idea of making idols was the beginning of fornication' — Wisdom 14 ties idolatry causally to sexual corruption and a flood of vices, exactly Paul's logic ('God gave them up... to uncleanness... vile passions'). High volume; the strongest single subtext for this pericope.

echoes.text: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.
echoes.note: 'Male and female' / 'natural function' presupposes the created-gender order of Genesis; sexual disorder figured as inversion of creation. Moderate verbal echo (physis vs. the Genesis pattern); thematic coherence high.

echoes.text: “‘You shall not lie with a man, as with a woman. That is detestable.
echoes.note: Same-sex relations as 'against nature' resonates with the Holiness Code prohibition tied to Gentile/Canaanite abomination. Conceptual coherence strong; verbal contact via LXX vocabulary moderate.

echoes.text: So I let them go after the stubbornness of their hearts, that they might walk in their own counsels.
echoes.note: 'So I gave them up (paredoka) to their own hearts' lust' is the divine-handing-over formula Paul triples ('God gave them up'). Strong verbal parallel to the paredoken auta refrain; judicial abandonment.

echoes.text: But before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sodom, surrounded the house, both young and old, all the people from every quarter. They called to Lot, and said to him, “Where are the men who came in to you this night? Bring them out to us, that we may have sex with them.” Lot went out to them to the door, and shut the door after him. He said, “Please, my brothers, don’t act so wickedly. See now, I have two virgin daughters. Please let me bring […]
echoes.note: Sodom as the archetype of disordered desire under judgment; figural background to the inflamed-lust description. Little verbal borrowing, contested.

echoes.text: Two sorts of men multiply sins, And the third will bring wrath: A hot mind, as a burning fire, will not be quenched till it be consumed: A fornicator in the body of his flesh will never cease till he has burned out the fire. All bread is sweet to a fornicator: He will not leave off till he die. A man that goes astray from his own bed, Saying in his heart, Who sees me? Darkness is round about me, and the walls hide me, And no man sees me; of whom am I […]
echoes.note: Sirach's catalogue of sexual sins and 'burning' desire offers a Second Temple parallel to 'burned in their lust.' Faint, contested verbal contact.

pericopes.text: Even as they refused to have God in their knowledge, God gave them up to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not fitting; being filled with all unrighteousness, sexual immorality, wickedness, covetousness, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil habits, secret slanderers, backbiters, hateful to God, insolent, haughty, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, without understanding, covenant breakers, without natural affection, unforgiving, unmerciful; who, knowing the ordinance of God, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but also approve of those who practice them.

echoes.text: Afterward it was not enough for them to go astray as touching the knowledge of God; But also, while they live in sore conflict through ignorance of him. That multitude of evils they call peace. For either slaughtering children in solemn rites, or celebrating secret mysteries, Or holding frantic revels of strange ordinances, No longer do they guard either life or purity of marriage, But one brings upon another either death by treachery, or anguish by […]
echoes.note: Wisdom's vice-catalogue flowing from idolatry (murder, deceit, corruption, faithlessness, defiling of life) closely parallels Paul's list and its idolatry-to-vice causal chain. High volume and recurrence; Paul's clearest model for the catalogue.

echoes.text: So I let them go after the stubbornness of their hearts, that they might walk in their own counsels.
echoes.note: Third 'God gave them up (to a reprobate mind)' continues the divine-abandonment formula of Ps 81:12 (LXX 80:13). Moderate verbal, strong thematic recurrence within the pericope-cluster.

echoes.text: They are all grievous rebels, going about with slanders; they are brass and iron: they all of them deal corruptly.
echoes.note: 'Slanderers... corrupters all' — prophetic vice description of a rebellious people; faint catalogue parallel.

echoes.text: Hear Yahweh’s word, you children of Israel; for Yahweh has a charge against the inhabitants of the land: “Indeed there is no truth, nor goodness, nor knowledge of God in the land. There is cursing, lying, murder, stealing, and committing adultery; they break boundaries, and bloodshed causes bloodshed.
echoes.note: 'No faithfulness... swearing, lying, murder, stealing, adultery' — prophetic indictment listing covenant breakdown, paralleling Paul's catalogue of murder/strife/deceit/covenant-breakers. Moderate conceptual coherence with the prophetic rib-pattern.

echoes.text: Yahweh saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of man’s heart was continually only evil.
echoes.note: 'Every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil' as the flood-era summary of total depravity; faint background to 'filled with all unrighteousness.' Little verbal contact, contested.

echoes.text: They have dealt corruptly with him. They are not his children, because of their defect. They are a perverse and crooked generation.
echoes.note: Song of Moses' description of a 'crooked and perverse generation... no faith in them' echoes the covenant-breaking, faithless terms of vv.31. Faint; Deut 32 recurs later in Romans.

echoes.text: For the temple was filled with riot and revellings by the heathen, who dallied with harlots, and had to do with women within the sacred precincts, and moreover brought inside things that were not befitting;
echoes.note: Second Temple moral-decline rhetoric pairing idolatry with comprehensive licentiousness; supports the 'approve of those who practice them' communal-corruption note. Faint parallel.

pericopes.text: Therefore you are without excuse, O man, whoever you are who judge. For in that which you judge another, you condemn yourself. For you who judge practice the same things. We know that the judgment of God is according to truth against those who practice such things. Do you think this, O man who judges those who practice such things, and do the same, that you will escape the judgment of God? Or do you despise the riches of his goodness, forbearance, and patience, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance? But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart you are treasuring up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath, revelation, and of the righteous judgment of God; who “will pay back to everyone according to their works:” to those who by patience in well-doing seek for glory, honor, and incorruptibility, eternal life; but to those who are self-seeking, and don’t obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, will be wrath and indignation, oppression and anguish, on every soul of man who works evil, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. But glory, honor, and peace go to every man who works good, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. For there is no partiality with God.

echoes.text: Also to you, Lord, belongs loving kindness, for you reward every man according to his work.
echoes.note: 2:6 'who will pay back to everyone according to their works' is a near-verbatim citation of Ps 62:12 (LXX 61:13), 'for you repay to each according to his work' — the foundational judgment maxim Paul deploys against the presumptuous judge.

echoes.text: If you say, “Behold, we didn’t know this”; doesn’t he who weighs the hearts consider it? He who keeps your soul, doesn’t he know it? Shall he not render to every man according to his work?
echoes.note: 2:6 equally cites Prov 24:12, 'will he not repay each according to his deeds?' — joint source with Ps 62:12; Prov adds the 'God who weighs the heart / does he not know?' frame that suits Paul's argument about secret motives (cf. 2:16).

echoes.text: For Yahweh your God, he is God of gods, and Lord of lords, the great God, the mighty, and the awesome, who doesn’t respect persons, nor takes reward.
echoes.note: 2:11 'there is no partiality with God' echoes Deut 10:17, 'God of gods... who shows no partiality (ou thaumazei prosopon) and takes no bribe' — the classic OT divine-impartiality formula underwriting Jew-and-Greek equality before judgment.

echoes.text: Now therefore let the fear of Yahweh be on you. Take heed and do it: for there is no iniquity with Yahweh our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of bribes.”
echoes.note: 2:11 also reflects Jehoshaphat's charge, 'with the LORD our God there is no injustice or partiality (prosopolempsia) or taking of bribes' — a near-technical Greek precedent for Paul's coined prosopolempsia.

echoes.text: Yahweh passed by before him, and proclaimed, “Yahweh! Yahweh, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth,
echoes.note: 2:4 'riches of his goodness, forbearance, and patience' draws on the covenant self-revelation 'a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger (makrothymos), abounding in steadfast love' — the divine attribute of forbearance Paul says should lead to repentance, not presumption.

echoes.text: But you have mercy on all men, because you have power to do all things, And you overlookest the sins of men to the end they may repent.
echoes.note: 2:4 'goodness... forbearance... leads to repentance' closely tracks Wisdom of Solomon 11:23, 'you overlook the sins of men so that they may repent,' and 12:10's gift of 'space for repentance' — Second Temple theology of divine patience Paul reuses and then turns critically against Israel.

echoes.text: “Isn’t this laid up in store with me, sealed up among my treasures? Vengeance is mine, and recompense, at the time when their foot slides; for the day of their calamity is at hand. Their doom rushes at them.”
echoes.note: 2:5 'treasuring up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath' echoes the Song of Moses, 'Is not this laid up in store with me, sealed up in my treasuries? Vengeance is mine,' the image of stored-up requital for a day of reckoning (Paul quotes the same verse at 12:19).

echoes.text: The great day of Yahweh is near. It is near, and hurries greatly, the voice of the day of Yahweh. The mighty man cries there bitterly. That day is a day of wrath, a day of distress and anguish, a day of trouble and ruin, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness, a day of the trumpet and alarm, against the fortified cities, and against the high battlements. I will bring distress on men, that they will walk like blind men, because they […]
echoes.note: 2:5 'day of wrath, revelation, and of the righteous judgment of God' draws on the Day-of-the-LORD oracle, 'that day is a day of wrath... of distress and anguish,' whose vocabulary (wrath, distress/anguish, cf. 2:9) saturates Paul's judgment scene.

echoes.text: Remember your servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Don’t look at the stubbornness of this people, nor at their wickedness, nor at their sin,
echoes.note: 2:5 'your hardness and unrepentant heart' may evoke the recurrent indictment of Israel's stubbornness (sklerokardia / hard neck), e.g. Deut 9:6,13,27; an echo Paul ironically applies to the self-confident judge.

echoes.text: I, Yahweh, search the mind, I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.
echoes.note: 2:6 repayment 'according to works' is reinforced by Jer 17:10, 'I the LORD search the heart... to give to each according to his ways, according to the fruit of his deeds' — joining heart-searching to works-recompense, both themes operative in Rom 2.

echoes.text: great in counsel, and mighty in work; whose eyes are open to all the ways of the sons of men, to give everyone according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings:
echoes.note: 2:6 'according to their works' resonates with Jer 32:19 (LXX 39:19), 'whose eyes are open to all the ways of men, to reward every man according to his ways and the fruit of his deeds' — another witness to the judgment-by-works topos.

echoes.text: For the work of a man he will render to him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.
echoes.note: 2:6 recompense by works also appears in Elihu's speech, 'for according to the work of a man he will repay him,' immediately followed (34:19) by God showing no partiality to princes — a striking pairing of Paul's two themes (works + impartiality).

echoes.text: As his mercy is great, so is his correction also: He judges a man according to his works. The sinner will not escape with his plunder; And the perseverance of the godly will not be frustrated. He will make room for every work of mercy; Each man will find according to his works.
echoes.note: 2:6 'according to works' is closely paralleled by Sirach 16:12-14, 'he judges a man according to his deeds... he makes room for every act of mercy; everyone receives according to his deeds' — Second Temple crystallization of the same recompense doctrine.

echoes.text: Think not to corrupt with gifts; for he will not receive them: And set not your mind on an unrighteous sacrifice; For the Lord is judge, And with him is no respect of persons. He will not accept any person against a poor man; And he will listen to the prayer of him that is wronged.
echoes.note: 2:11 'no partiality' is anticipated by Sirach 35:12-13 (LXX 35:15-16), 'the Lord is the judge, and with him is no partiality; he will not show partiality to the poor' — Second Temple restatement of the impartiality formula in a judgment context.

pericopes.text: For as many as have sinned without law will also perish without the law. As many as have sinned under the law will be judged by the law. For it isn’t the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but the doers of the law will be justified (for when Gentiles who don’t have the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves, in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their thoughts among themselves accusing or else excusing them) in the day when God will judge the secrets of men, according to my Good News, by Jesus Christ.

echoes.text: You shall therefore keep my statutes and my ordinances; which if a man does, he shall live in them. I am Yahweh.
echoes.note: 2:13 'the doers of the law will be justified' echoes the Torah principle 'the person who does them shall live by them' — the do-and-live logic (which Paul cites directly at 10:5; Gal 3:12) standing behind 'doers' over 'hearers.'

echoes.text: Now, Israel, listen to the statutes and to the ordinances, which I teach you, to do them; that you may live, and go in and possess the land which Yahweh, the God of your fathers, gives you.
echoes.note: 2:13 hearing-versus-doing reflects Moses' charge to 'listen (hear) to the statutes... and do them, that you may live,' the Deuteronomic pairing of shema and asah that Paul splits to indict mere hearers.

echoes.text: For this commandment which I command you this day is not too hard for you or too distant. It is not in heaven, that you should say, “Who will go up for us to heaven, and bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?” Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say, “Who will go over the sea for us, and bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?” But the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, that you may do […]
echoes.note: 2:14-15 Gentiles 'a law to themselves' with the law's work 'in their hearts' faintly recalls Deut 30:11-14, 'the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, so that you can do it' — the nearness/internality of the commandment (Paul quotes this at 10:6-8), here generalized to conscience.

echoes.text: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says Yahweh: I will put my law in their inward parts, and in their heart will I write it; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people:
echoes.note: 2:15 'the work of the law written in their hearts' verbally echoes the new-covenant promise 'I will put my law within them, and on their hearts I will write it' — though Paul applies the imagery to Gentiles' moral intuition rather than Israel's eschatological renewal, the borrowing is deliberate and ironic.

echoes.text: For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it is good, or whether it is evil.
echoes.note: 2:16 'God will judge the secrets of men' draws on Qoheleth's conclusion, 'God will bring every deed into judgment, with every secret thing, whether good or evil' — secret-deed judgment as the climax of the wisdom tradition.

echoes.text: won’t God search this out? For he knows the secrets of the heart.
echoes.note: 2:16 judging 'the secrets of men' echoes Ps 44:21 (LXX 43:22), 'would not God discover this? For he knows the secrets of the heart' — divine knowledge of hidden things grounding the verdict.

echoes.text: For wisdom is a spirit that loves man, And she will not hold a blasphemer guiltless for his lips; Because God bears witness of his reins, And is a true overseer of his heart, And a hearer of his tongue: Because the spirit of the Lord has filled the world, And that which holds all things together has knowledge of every voice. Therefore no man that utters unrighteous things will be unseen; Neither will Justice, when it convicts, pass him by. For in the […]
echoes.note: 2:16 'judge the secrets' parallels Wisdom of Solomon 1:6-9, 'God is witness of his inmost feelings... a hearing reaches the Lord... and the report of his words comes to the Lord to convict him of his lawless deeds' — Second Temple scrutiny of inner thoughts at judgment.

echoes.text: But Yahweh said to Samuel, “Don’t look on his face, or on the height of his stature; because I have rejected him: for I see not as man sees; for man looks at the outward appearance, but Yahweh looks at the heart.”
echoes.note: 2:16 God judging hidden 'secrets' resonates with 'man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart' — the principle of inward divine sight underlying Paul's contrast between outward and inward (developed at 2:28-29).

echoes.text: I, Yahweh, search the mind, I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.
echoes.note: 2:16 secret-judgment overlaps with Jer 17:10, 'I the LORD search the heart and test the mind' — heart-searching paired with works-recompense, already noted at 2:6 and reinforcing the pericope's frame.

pericopes.text: Indeed you bear the name of a Jew, and rest on the law, and glory in God, and know his will, and approve the things that are excellent, being instructed out of the law, and are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light to those who are in darkness, a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of babies, having in the law the form of knowledge and of the truth. You therefore who teach another, don’t you teach yourself? You who preach that a man shouldn’t steal, do you steal? You who say a man shouldn’t commit adultery. Do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples? You who glory in the law, through your disobedience of the law do you dishonor God? For “the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you,” just as it is written.

echoes.text: “Now therefore, what do I do here,” says Yahweh, “seeing that my people are taken away for nothing? Those who rule over them mock,” says Yahweh, “and my name continually all the day is blasphemed.
echoes.note: 2:24 'the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you, just as it is written' is an explicit formula-citation of Isa 52:5 LXX, 'because of you my name is continually blasphemed among the nations' — Paul's clinching scriptural proof of the indictment.

echoes.text: When they came to the nations, where they went, they profaned my holy name; in that men said of them, These are the people of Yahweh, and are gone out of his land. But I had respect for my holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations, where they went. Therefore tell the house of Israel, Thus says the Lord Yahweh: I don’t do this for your sake, house of Israel, but for my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations, where […]
echoes.note: 2:24 the profaning of God's name among the nations is reinforced by Ezek 36:20-23, 'they profaned my holy name... wherever they came among the nations' — the same prophetic logic (Israel's conduct dishonoring God before the Gentiles), and Ezek 36's heart/spirit renewal also feeds 2:29.

echoes.text: But to the wicked God says, “What right do you have to declare my statutes, that you have taken my covenant on your lips, since you hate instruction, and throw my words behind you? When you saw a thief, you consented with him, and have participated with adulterers. “You give your mouth to evil. Your tongue frames deceit. You sit and speak against your brother. You slander your own mother’s son. You have done these things, and I kept silent. You thought […]
echoes.note: 2:21-22 'you who teach another, don't you teach yourself? You who preach don't steal, do you steal?... commit adultery?' closely mirrors Ps 50:16-21 (LXX 49), 'what right have you to recite my statutes...? you keep company with thieves... and with adulterers' — God's rebuke of the hypocrite who recites the law while breaking it.

echoes.text: “I, Yahweh, have called you in righteousness, and will hold your hand, and will keep you, and make you a covenant for the people, as a light for the nations; to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
echoes.note: 2:19 'a guide of the blind, a light to those in darkness' draws on the Servant's vocation 'a light to the nations, to open the eyes that are blind, to bring out... those who sit in darkness' — Israel's self-understanding as light to the Gentiles, which Paul ironizes.

echoes.text: yes, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give you for a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.”
echoes.note: 2:19 'a light to those in darkness' also echoes Isa 49:6, 'I will make you a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth' — the Servant-Israel light-to-Gentiles motif Paul invokes only to expose the teacher's failure.

echoes.text: Who is blind, but my servant? Or who is as deaf as my messenger whom I send? Who is as blind as he who is at peace, and as blind as Yahweh’s servant?
echoes.note: 2:19 the irony deepens with Isa 42:19, 'who is blind but my servant... who is blind as the dedicated one?' — the would-be guide of the blind is himself the blind servant; a faint counter-echo within the same Isaianic context.

echoes.text: You shall burn the engraved images of their gods with fire. You shall not covet the silver or the gold that is on them, nor take it for yourself, lest you be snared in it; for it is an abomination to Yahweh your God. You shall not bring an abomination into your house, and become a devoted thing like it. You shall utterly detest it, and you shall utterly abhor it; for it is a devoted thing.
echoes.note: 2:22 'you who abhor idols, do you rob temples?' reflects Deut 7:25-26, 'the carved images of their gods you shall burn... you shall utterly abhor it (bdelysse), for it is an abomination' — the very verb of abhorring idols (bdelyssomenos) Paul uses, sharpening the charge of temple-robbing inconsistency.

pericopes.text: For circumcision indeed profits, if you are a doer of the law, but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision. If therefore the uncircumcised keep the ordinances of the law, won’t his uncircumcision be accounted as circumcision? Won’t the uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfills the law, judge you, who with the letter and circumcision are a transgressor of the law? For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh; but he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit not in the letter; whose praise is not from men, but from God.

echoes.text: Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiff-necked.
echoes.note: 2:29 'circumcision is that of the heart' directly echoes Moses' command 'circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no longer stubborn' — the foundational text spiritualizing circumcision (note the proximity to Deut 10:17's impartiality, used at 2:11).

echoes.text: Yahweh your God will circumcise your heart, and the heart of your seed, to love Yahweh your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, that you may live.
echoes.note: 2:29 heart-circumcision in the Spirit draws on Deut 30:6, 'the LORD your God will circumcise your heart... so that you will love the LORD' — the promised divine (eschatological, Spirit-effected) circumcision, matching Paul's 'in the spirit not the letter.'

echoes.text: Circumcise yourselves to Yahweh, and take away the foreskins of your heart, you men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem; lest my wrath go out like fire, and burn so that no one can quench it, because of the evil of your doings.
echoes.note: 2:29 'circumcision of the heart' echoes Jer 4:4, 'circumcise yourselves to the LORD; remove the foreskin of your hearts' — prophetic demand for inward circumcision lest wrath go forth, fitting Paul's wrath-and-heart argument.

echoes.text: Behold, the days come, says Yahweh, that I will punish all those who are circumcised in uncircumcision: Egypt, and Judah, and Edom, and the children of Ammon, and Moab, and all that have the corners of their hair cut off, who dwell in the wilderness; for all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in heart.
echoes.note: 2:25-29 the worthlessness of fleshly circumcision without obedience reflects Jer 9:25-26, 'I will punish all who are circumcised merely in the flesh... for all these nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart' — exactly Paul's leveling of circumcised and uncircumcised by the heart criterion.

echoes.text: I also walked contrary to them, and brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled, and they then accept the punishment of their iniquity;
echoes.note: 2:29 inward circumcision recalls Lev 26:41, 'if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled and they make amends for their iniquity' — the Holiness Code's notion of an uncircumcised heart needing humbling, a Torah basis for the heart/flesh distinction.

echoes.text: in that you have brought in foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary, to profane it, even my house, when you offer my bread, the fat and the blood, and they have broken my covenant, to add to all your abominations. You have not performed the duty of my holy things; but you have set performers of my duty in my sanctuary for yourselves. Thus says the Lord Yahweh, No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and […]
echoes.note: 2:25-29 the pairing 'uncircumcised in heart and flesh' appears in Ezek 44:7-9 barring those 'uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh' from the sanctuary — the dual (heart/flesh) circumcision distinction Paul exploits.

echoes.text: I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: 2:29 'in the spirit, not in the letter' echoes the new-heart promise, 'I will give you a new heart... and put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes' — Spirit-wrought interior obedience over external observance.

echoes.text: God said to Abraham, “As for you, you will keep my covenant, you and your seed after you throughout their generations. This is my covenant, which you shall keep, between me and you and your seed after you. Every male among you shall be circumcised. You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin. It will be a token of the covenant between me and you. He who is eight days old will be circumcised among you, every male throughout your generations, he […]
echoes.note: 2:25-29 the whole argument presupposes and reinterprets the Abrahamic covenant of circumcision in the flesh (Gen 17, 'every male shall be circumcised... in your flesh an everlasting covenant') — Paul figurally relocates the 'everlasting covenant' sign from flesh to heart/Spirit.

echoes.text: She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “This time will I praise Yahweh.” Therefore she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing.
echoes.note: 2:29 'whose praise is not from men but from God' likely plays on the etymology of 'Jew' (Judah/Yehudah), named in Gen 29:35 when Leah says 'this time I will praise the LORD' — the true Jew is the one of genuine praise, a Hebrew wordplay (Judah = praise; cf. Gen 49:8).

pericopes.text: Then what advantage does the Jew have? Or what is the profit of circumcision? Much in every way! Because first of all, they were entrusted with the oracles of God. For what if some were without faith? Will their lack of faith nullify the faithfulness of God? May it never be! Yes, let God be found true, but every man a liar. As it is written, “That you might be justified in your words, and might prevail when you come into judgment.” But if our unrighteousness commends the righteousness of God, what will we say? Is God unrighteous who inflicts wrath? I speak like men do. May it never be! For then how will God judge the world? For if the truth of God through my lie abounded to his glory, why am I also still judged as a sinner? Why not (as we are slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say), “Let us do evil, that good may come?” Those who say so are justly condemned.

echoes.text: Against you, and you only, have I sinned, and done that which is evil in your sight; that you may be proved right when you speak, and justified when you judge.
echoes.note: Verbatim citation introduced by 'as it is written' in 3:4: 'that you might be justified in your words, and might prevail when you come into judgment' = LXX Psalm 50:6, David's confession in the Miserere. Paul deploys it to vindicate God's righteousness against human faithlessness: God is justified (proven right) precisely when humans are shown liars.
echoes.lxxText: Against thee only have I sinned, and done evil before thee: that thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and mightest overcome when thou art judged.

echoes.text: For what great nation is there, that has a god so near to them, as Yahweh our God is whenever we call on him? What great nation is there, that has statutes and ordinances so righteous as all this law, which I set before you this day?
echoes.note: The 'advantage of the Jew' and being 'entrusted with the oracles of God' (3:1-2) echoes Israel's unique covenantal privilege of possessing God's statutes and nearness, the defining boast of Deuteronomy 4:7-8. Paul concedes this advantage before relativizing it.

echoes.text: He said of his father, and of his mother, ‘I have not seen him.’ He didn’t acknowledge his brothers, nor did he know his own children; for they have observed your word, and keep your covenant.
echoes.note: Israel as guardian of 'the oracles/words of God' (3:2) faintly recalls Levi keeping God's word and covenant; the 'logia tou theou' language draws on the deposit-of-the-law tradition.

echoes.text: God is not a man, that he should lie, nor the son of man, that he should repent. Has he said, and will he not do it? Or has he spoken, and will he not make it good?
echoes.note: 'Let God be found true, but every man a liar' (3:4) restates Balaam's axiom that God is not a man that he should lie; the contrast between divine truthfulness and human falsehood is the same theological commitment.

echoes.text: I said in my haste, “All men are liars.”
echoes.note: 'Every man a liar' (3:4) is the psalmist's verbatim verdict, 'all men are liars' (LXX Psalm 115:2). Paul fuses it with the Psalm 51 citation to dramatize the truth-of-God / lie-of-humanity antithesis.

echoes.text: Be it far from you to do things like that, to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be like the wicked. May that be far from you. Shouldn’t the Judge of all the earth do right?”
echoes.note: 'How will God judge the world?' (3:6) invokes Abraham's appeal to the Judge of all the earth who must do right; God's universal judicial competence is the unquestionable premise that secures his righteousness.

echoes.text: Yet the number of the children of Israel will be as the sand of the sea, which can’t be measured nor numbered; and it will come to pass that, in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’
echoes.note: The faithfulness-of-God-despite-Israel's-faithlessness theme (3:3) anticipates the Hosea citations Paul will marshal in Romans 9; God's covenant fidelity outlasts the people's apistia.

pericopes.text: What then? Are we better than they? No, in no way. For we previously warned both Jews and Greeks, that they are all under sin. As it is written, “There is no one righteous; no, not one. There is no one who understands. There is no one who seeks after God. They have all turned aside. They have together become unprofitable. There is no one who does good, no, not so much as one.” “Their throat is an open tomb. With their tongues they have used deceit.” “The poison of vipers is under their lips”; “whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.” “Their feet are swift to shed blood. Destruction and misery are in their ways. The way of peace, they haven’t known.” “There is no fear of God before their eyes.” Now we know that whatever things the law says, it speaks to those who are under the law, that every mouth may be closed, and all the world may be brought under the judgment of God. Because by the works of the law, no flesh will be justified in his sight. For through the law comes the knowledge of sin.

echoes.text: The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt. They have done abominable works. There is no one who does good. Yahweh looked down from heaven on the children of men, to see if there were any who understood, who sought after God. They have all gone aside. They have together become corrupt. There is no one who does good, no, not one.
echoes.note: Head of the catena (3:10-12): 'There is none righteous... none who understands... none who seeks God; all have turned aside, together become worthless; none does good, not one.' This is a near-verbatim chain from LXX Psalm 13:1-3, the fool who says there is no God. Paul opens his 'as it is written' string here.

echoes.text: Surely there is not a righteous man on earth, who does good and doesn’t sin.
echoes.note: 'There is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins' supplies the same universal-sin thesis as the catena's opening 'none righteous... none does good' (3:10-12); a wisdom-tradition reinforcement of the Psalm 14 verdict.

echoes.text: For there is no faithfulness in their mouth. Their heart is destruction. Their throat is an open tomb. They flatter with their tongue.
echoes.note: Catena member at 3:13a: 'Their throat is an open tomb; with their tongues they have practiced deceit' = LXX Psalm 5:10, verbatim. Begins the catena's catalogue of speech-organs (throat, tongue, lips, mouth).

echoes.text: They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent. Viper’s poison is under their lips. Selah.
echoes.note: Catena member at 3:13b: 'The poison of asps/vipers is under their lips' = LXX Psalm 139:4, verbatim. Continues the speech catalogue from lips.

echoes.text: His mouth is full of cursing, deceit, and oppression. Under his tongue is mischief and iniquity.
echoes.note: Catena member at 3:14: 'whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness' draws on LXX Psalm 9:28 (Psalm 10:7 MT), 'his mouth is full of cursing and deceit and oppression.' Completes the mouth-cursing item of the speech catalogue.

echoes.text: Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood: their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity; desolation and destruction are in their paths. The way of peace they don’t know; and there is no justice in their goings: they have made them crooked paths; whoever goes therein does not know peace.
echoes.note: Catena member at 3:15-17: 'Their feet are swift to shed blood; destruction and misery are in their ways; and the way of peace they have not known' = Isaiah 59:7-8, the prophet's indictment that justice and peace are absent. The lone prophetic link in the otherwise psalmic chain; shifts from speech to feet/ways.

echoes.text: for their feet run to evil. They hurry to shed blood.
echoes.note: 'Their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood' parallels 3:15 ('their feet are swift to shed blood') and overlaps Isaiah 59:7; some hold Proverbs 1:16 contributes to or doubles the source of the feet-shedding-blood clause.

echoes.text: An oracle is within my heart about the disobedience of the wicked: “There is no fear of God before his eyes.”
echoes.note: Catena's climactic capstone at 3:18: 'There is no fear of God before their eyes' = LXX Psalm 35:2, verbatim. The chain closes by returning the indictment to its root (fear of God / eyes), inclusio with the opening 'none seeks God.'

echoes.text: Don’t enter into judgment with your servant, for in your sight no man living is righteous.
echoes.note: 3:20: 'by works of the law no flesh will be justified in his sight' adapts LXX Psalm 142:2, 'do not enter into judgment with your servant, for in your sight no living one shall be justified.' Paul adds 'by works of the law' but the 'no flesh justified before you' core is verbatim from the psalmist.

echoes.text: God saw the earth, and saw that it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth.
echoes.note: 'All have turned aside, together become corrupt/worthless' (3:12) faintly recalls the Flood verdict that all flesh had corrupted its way on earth; both render a totalizing 'all flesh' depravity.

echoes.text: No one sues in righteousness, and no one pleads in truth: they trust in vanity, and speak lies; they conceive mischief, and give birth to iniquity.
echoes.note: Beyond the quoted 59:7-8, the wider Isaiah 59 oracle ('none calls for justice... they conceive mischief') colors the catena's portrait; Paul likely has the whole indictment-of-no-righteousness pericope in view.

echoes.text: “Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?
echoes.note: 'How can a man be righteous before God?' anticipates 3:20's 'no flesh justified in his sight'; the forensic impossibility of human self-justification before God is a shared wisdom premise.

pericopes.text: But now apart from the law, a righteousness of God has been revealed, being testified by the law and the prophets; even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ to all and on all those who believe. For there is no distinction, for all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God; being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus; whom God sent to be an atoning sacrifice, through faith in his blood, for a demonstration of his righteousness through the passing over of prior sins, in God’s forbearance; to demonstrate his righteousness at this present time; that he might himself be just, and the justifier of him who has faith in Jesus. Where then is the boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? Of works? No, but by a law of faith. We maintain therefore that a man is justified by faith apart from the works of the law. Or is God the God of Jews only? Isn’t he the God of Gentiles also? Yes, of Gentiles also, since indeed there is one God who will justify the circumcised by faith, and the uncircumcised through faith. Do we then nullify the law through faith? May it never be! No, we establish the law.

echoes.text: Behold, his soul is puffed up. It is not upright in him, but the righteous will live by his faith.
echoes.note: The thesis of 'righteousness of God through faith' (3:21-22) carries forward the programmatic citation of 1:17, 'the righteous shall live by faith'; the faith-righteousness axis here is governed by Habakkuk even without re-quotation.

echoes.text: My righteousness is near, my salvation has gone out, and my arms shall judge the peoples; the islands shall wait for me, and on my arm shall they trust. Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look on the earth beneath; for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment; and those who dwell therein shall die in the same way: but my salvation shall be forever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished. “Listen to me, […]
echoes.note: 'A righteousness of God has been revealed' (3:21) echoes Deutero-Isaiah's repeated proclamation that God's righteousness/salvation 'draws near' and 'is revealed'; the apocalyptic unveiling of divine sedaqah is Isaianic.

echoes.text: Yahweh has made known his salvation. He has openly shown his righteousness in the sight of the nations.
echoes.note: 'The LORD has made known his salvation; he has revealed his righteousness in the sight of the nations' is a close template for 3:21-22: God's righteousness now revealed to all who believe, Jew and Gentile alike.

echoes.text: and he shall put the incense on the fire before Yahweh, that the cloud of the incense may cover the mercy seat that is on the testimony, so that he will not die. He shall take some of the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it with his finger on the mercy seat on the east; and before the mercy seat he shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times. “Then he shall kill the goat of the sin offering, that is for the people, and bring his blood […]
echoes.note: Christ set forth as 'hilasterion' / atoning sacrifice 'in his blood' (3:25) typologically fulfills the Day of Atonement mercy seat (kapporeth, LXX hilasterion) sprinkled with blood; the temple atonement apparatus prefigures the cross.

echoes.text: You shall make a mercy seat of pure gold. Two and a half cubits shall be its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth. You shall make two cherubim of hammered gold. You shall make them at the two ends of the mercy seat. Make one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end. You shall make the cherubim on its two ends of one piece with the mercy seat. The cherubim shall spread out their wings upward, covering the mercy seat with their wings, […]
echoes.note: The 'hilasterion' of 3:25 is the very term LXX uses for the mercy seat / cover of the ark where God meets Israel; Paul presents Christ as the eschatological place of propitiation, fulfilling the ark typology.

echoes.text: After the suffering of his soul, he will see the light and be satisfied. My righteous servant will justify many by the knowledge of himself; and he will bear their iniquities. Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the plunder with the strong; because he poured out his soul to death, and was numbered with the transgressors; yet he bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.
echoes.note: Justification 'freely by his grace through the redemption in Christ Jesus' and the atoning-blood demonstration of righteousness (3:24-25) echoes the Servant who 'makes many righteous' by bearing sin; the vicarious sin-bearing undergirds Paul's atonement language.

echoes.text: Hear, Israel: Yahweh is our God. Yahweh is one.
echoes.note: 'There is one God who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith' (3:30) grounds itself in the Shema's 'the LORD is one'; Paul turns Israel's monotheistic confession into the warrant for one way of justification for Jew and Gentile.

echoes.text: God said to Abraham, “As for you, you will keep my covenant, you and your seed after you throughout their generations. This is my covenant, which you shall keep, between me and you and your seed after you. Every male among you shall be circumcised. You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin. It will be a token of the covenant between me and you. He who is eight days old will be circumcised among you, every male throughout your generations, he […]
echoes.note: The circumcised/uncircumcised distinction relativized in 3:29-30 presupposes the Abrahamic circumcision covenant; Paul prepares the ground for Romans 4's argument that Abraham was reckoned righteous before circumcision.

echoes.text: Yahweh passed by before him, and proclaimed, “Yahweh! Yahweh, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth, keeping loving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity and disobedience and sin; and that will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, and on the children’s children, on the third and on the fourth generation.”
echoes.note: God's 'forbearance' and 'passing over of former sins' (3:25-26) draws on the covenant formula of the LORD slow to anger, forgiving iniquity yet not clearing the guilty; Paul shows how God can pass over sins and still be just.

echoes.text: Thus says Yahweh, Don’t let the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, don’t let the rich man glory in his riches; but let him who glories glory in this, that he has understanding, and knows me, that I am Yahweh who exercises loving kindness, justice, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, says Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'Where then is boasting? It is excluded' (3:27) echoes Jeremiah's prohibition of boasting in wisdom, might, or riches, allowing boasting only in knowing the LORD who does righteousness; Paul transposes the anti-boast theme to works of law.

echoes.text: Declare and present it. Yes, let them take counsel together. Who has shown this from ancient time? Who has declared it of old? Haven’t I, Yahweh? There is no other God besides me, a just God and a Savior; There is no one besides me. “Look to me, and be saved, all the ends of the earth; for I am God, and there is no other. I have sworn by myself, the word has gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and will not return, that to me every knee shall bow, every […]
echoes.note: 'A righteous God and a Savior... in the LORD all the offspring of Israel shall be justified,' with every nation turning to the one God, undergirds 3:26-30: God just and justifier, one God of Jews and Gentiles.

echoes.text: He believed in Yahweh; and he reckoned it to him for righteousness.
echoes.note: 'Justified by faith apart from works of the law' (3:28) anticipates and is governed by the Abraham-reckoned-righteous text Paul will quote in 4:3; the faith-reckoning principle is already operative here.

pericopes.text: What then will we say that Abraham, our forefather, has found according to the flesh? For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about, but not toward God. For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness.” Now to him who works, the reward is not counted as grace, but as something owed. But to him who doesn’t work, but believes in him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is accounted for righteousness. Even as David also pronounces blessing on the man to whom God counts righteousness apart from works, “Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man whom the Lord will by no means charge with sin.”

echoes.text: He believed in Yahweh; and he reckoned it to him for righteousness.
echoes.note: The governing text of the entire chapter, quoted verbatim in 4:3 ('Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness'). Paul launches a sustained midrash on this single verse, returning to its key term 'accounted/reckoned' (LXX elogisthe) throughout. Maximum volume and recurrence.

echoes.text: Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man to whom Yahweh doesn’t impute iniquity, in whose spirit there is no deceit.
echoes.note: Quoted verbatim in 4:7-8 ('Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven... Blessed is the man whom the Lord will by no means charge with sin'). Paul attributes it to David and links it to Genesis 15:6 by gezerah shawah on the shared verb 'reckon/charge' (logizomai): the man to whom the Lord does NOT reckon sin = the man to whom God reckons righteousness apart from works.

echoes.text: After these things Yahweh’s word came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Don’t be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your exceedingly great reward.”
echoes.note: Paul's argument from 'reward' (misthos) in 4:4 ('to him who works, the reward is not counted as grace') draws on the immediate context of Genesis 15:6, where God tells Abraham in 15:1 'your reward shall be very great.' Paul reads the surrounding promise narrative, not just the proof-text.

echoes.text: “Keep far from a false charge, and don’t kill the innocent and righteous: for I will not justify the wicked.
echoes.note: God's self-description as one who 'justifies the ungodly' (4:5) deliberately inverts the legal maxim of Exodus 23:7 LXX, 'you shall not justify the ungodly' (ou dikaioseis ton asebe). Paul scandalously predicates of God the very act forbidden to human judges, signaling that justification is grace, not legal verdict on merit.

echoes.text: He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the righteous, both of them alike are an abomination to Yahweh.
echoes.note: Reinforces the same forensic reversal: Proverbs 17:15 calls 'he who justifies the wicked' an abomination to the Lord. Paul's phrase 'justifies the ungodly' (4:5) is a calculated provocation against this wisdom commonplace. Thematically coherent but verbally less direct than Exodus 23:7; marked contested.

echoes.text: Abraham was a great father of a multitude of nations; And there was none found like him in glory; Who kept the law of the Most High, And was taken into covenant with him: In his flesh he established the covenant; And when he was proved, he was found faithful. Therefore he assured him by an oath, That the nations should be blessed in his seed; That he would multiply him as the dust of the earth, And exalt his seed as the stars, And cause them to inherit […]
echoes.note: Second Temple reception of Abraham: 'Abraham was the great father of a multitude of nations... he kept the law of the Most High... therefore the Lord assured him by an oath that nations would be blessed through his offspring.' Sirach reads Abraham's righteousness as covenant-keeping/Torah-obedience, the very reading Paul argues against. A contested background echo: Paul writes with such Second Temple Abraham-as-law-keeper tradition in view.

echoes.text: Was not Abraham found faithful in temptation, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness?
echoes.note: 1 Maccabees 2:52 ('Was not Abraham found faithful when tested, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness?') itself cites Genesis 15:6 but fuses it with the Aqedah (Genesis 22) to make faith = proven works/faithfulness under testing. This is the foil for Paul's whole argument that the reckoning preceded and excluded works. Strong verbal overlap with the catchphrase 'reckoned... as righteousness'; marked contested as reception-background rather than source.

echoes.text: Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you; for when he was but one I called him, and I blessed him, and made him many.
echoes.note: 'Abraham, our forefather' (4:1) may echo Isaiah 51:2, 'Look to Abraham your father... for he was but one when I called him,' a text about Abraham as progenitor of a numerous people from a single ancestor — the theme Paul develops in 4:16-18. Faint; thematic only.

pericopes.text: Is this blessing then pronounced on the circumcised, or on the uncircumcised also? For we say that faith was accounted to Abraham for righteousness. How then was it counted? When he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision. He received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had while he was in uncircumcision, that he might be the father of all those who believe, though they might be in uncircumcision, that righteousness might also be accounted to them. He is the father of circumcision to those who not only are of the circumcision, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had in uncircumcision.

echoes.text: This is my covenant, which you shall keep, between me and you and your seed after you. Every male among you shall be circumcised. You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin. It will be a token of the covenant between me and you.
echoes.note: Paul's argument that Abraham 'received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith' (4:11) directly invokes Genesis 17:10-11, where circumcision is instituted as 'a sign of the covenant.' Paul takes the Genesis term 'sign' and subordinates it to the faith of Genesis 15, which chronologically preceded it.

echoes.text: He believed in Yahweh; and he reckoned it to him for righteousness.
echoes.note: The pericope hangs entirely on the chronology of Genesis: faith reckoned (15:6) came BEFORE circumcision (chapter 17). 4:9-10 re-quotes 'faith was accounted to Abraham for righteousness' and asks whether the reckoning happened in circumcision or uncircumcision — recurrence of the governing text used as a temporal argument.

echoes.text: Neither will your name any more be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham; for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.
echoes.note: 'That he might be the father of all those who believe' (4:11) and 'the father of circumcision' (4:12) anticipate the quotation of Genesis 17:5 in 4:17, reading Abraham's universal fatherhood out of the Genesis covenant promise. The 'father of many nations' motif governs the circumcised/uncircumcised dual fatherhood here.

pericopes.text: For the promise to Abraham and to his seed that he should be heir of the world wasn’t through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith is made void, and the promise is made of no effect. For the law works wrath, for where there is no law, neither is there disobedience. For this cause it is of faith, that it may be according to grace, to the end that the promise may be sure to all the seed, not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all.

echoes.text: I will give to you, and to your seed after you, the land where you are traveling, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession. I will be their God.”
echoes.note: 'The promise to Abraham and to his seed that he should be heir of the world' (4:13) universalizes the land-inheritance promises of Genesis (17:8 'I will give to you and your offspring... all the land of Canaan for an everlasting possession'; cf. 13:15; 15:7). Paul expands the territorial 'land' to 'the world' (kosmos), a move grounded in the cosmic scope of the promise.

echoes.text: that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your seed greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your seed will possess the gate of his enemies. All the nations of the earth will be blessed by your seed, because you have obeyed my voice.”
echoes.note: The promise to Abraham 'and to his seed' (4:13) echoes the oath of Genesis 22:17-18, 'I will multiply your seed... and in your seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed,' which links seed, multiplication, and universal blessing — the basis for 'heir of the world.' The word 'seed' (sperma) is the Genesis catchword Paul foregrounds.

echoes.text: Therefore he assured him by an oath, That the nations should be blessed in his seed; That he would multiply him as the dust of the earth, And exalt his seed as the stars, And cause them to inherit from sea to sea, And from the River to the utmost part of the earth.
echoes.note: The 'heir of the world' expansion has a Second Temple precedent in Sirach 44:21, where God promises Abraham 'to give them an inheritance from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth' — already enlarging the land to global scope. A contested background echo for Paul's kosmos language.

echoes.text: He said to him, “I am Yahweh who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give you this land to inherit it.”
echoes.note: Genesis 15:7 ('I am the Lord who brought you out... to give you this land to inherit it'), within the same chapter as 15:6, supplies the inheritance vocabulary Paul universalizes in 'heir of the world.' Faint; reinforces that Paul reads the whole Genesis 15 unit.

pericopes.text: As it is written, “I have made you a father of many nations.” This is in the presence of him whom he believed: God, who gives life to the dead, and calls the things that are not, as though they were. Who in hope believed against hope, to the end that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken, “So will your seed be.” Without being weakened in faith, he didn’t consider his own body, already having been worn out, (he being about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah’s womb. Yet, looking to the promise of God, he didn’t waver through unbelief, but grew strong through faith, giving glory to God, and being fully assured that what he had promised, he was also able to perform. Therefore it also was “reckoned to him for righteousness.”

echoes.text: Neither will your name any more be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham; for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.
echoes.note: Quoted verbatim with the introductory formula 'As it is written' in 4:17: 'I have made you a father of many nations' (Genesis 17:5 LXX, 'patera pollon ethnon tetheika se'). Paul reads the perfect tense ('I HAVE made') as already-accomplished divine speech that calls the not-yet into being.

echoes.text: Yahweh brought him outside, and said, “Look now toward the sky, and count the stars, if you are able to count them.” He said to Abram, “So will your seed be.”
echoes.note: Quoted verbatim in 4:18: 'So will your seed be' (Genesis 15:5 LXX, 'houtos estai to sperma sou'), the star-promise spoken immediately before Genesis 15:6. Paul binds the two halves of Genesis 15 together: the promise (v.5) and Abraham's believing response reckoned as righteousness (v.6).

echoes.text: Then Abraham fell on his face, and laughed, and said in his heart, “Will a child be born to him who is one hundred years old? Will Sarah, who is ninety years old, give birth?”
echoes.note: 'He being about a hundred years old, and the deadness of Sarah's womb' (4:19) draws directly on Genesis 17:17, where Abraham, told he will have a son, says 'Shall a child be born to him who is a hundred years old? And shall Sarah, who is ninety, bear?' Paul reuses the numeric detail and the implied biological impossibility.

echoes.text: Now Abraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in age. Sarah had passed the age of childbearing. Sarah laughed within herself, saying, “After I have grown old will I have pleasure, my lord being old also?”
echoes.note: 'The deadness of Sarah's womb' and Abraham's 'body already worn out' (4:19) echo Genesis 18:11-12: 'it had ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women,' and Sarah's words 'After I am worn out (LXX katetribe), shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?' Paul's 'worn out' (nenekromenon/already dead) language tracks the Genesis 18 description of both spouses' exhaustion.

echoes.text: Is anything too hard for Yahweh? At the set time I will return to you, when the season comes round, and Sarah will have a son.”
echoes.note: Abraham 'being fully assured that what he had promised, he was also able to perform' (4:21) answers the rhetorical question of Genesis 18:14, 'Is anything too hard for the Lord? At the appointed time I will return... and Sarah shall have a son.' Paul converts the LORD's question into Abraham's confident assent — God's power over the impossible.

echoes.text: “Yahweh kills, and makes alive. He brings down to Sheol, and brings up.
echoes.note: 'God, who gives life to the dead' (4:17) draws on the scriptural confession of God as life-giver, e.g. 1 Samuel 2:6 (Hannah), 'The Lord kills and makes alive; he brings down to Sheol and raises up.' This is the standard OT idiom Paul applies to both Isaac's miraculous conception and the resurrection.

echoes.text: “See now that I myself am he. There is no god with me. I kill and I make alive. I wound and I heal. There is no one who can deliver out of my hand.
echoes.note: 'God, who gives life to the dead' (4:17) also resonates with Deuteronomy 32:39, 'I kill and I make alive; I wound and I heal,' a foundational text for God's sole power over death and life. Reinforces the same divine attribute Paul predicates.

echoes.text: The hand of Yahweh was on me, and he brought me out in the Spirit of Yahweh, and set me down in the midst of the valley; and it was full of bones. He caused me to pass by them all around: and behold, there were very many in the open valley; and behold, they were very dry. He said to me, Son of man, can these bones live? I answered, Lord Yahweh, you know. Again he said to me, Prophesy over these bones, and tell them, you dry bones, hear Yahweh’s word. Thus […]
echoes.note: 'God, who gives life to the dead' (4:17) may figurally echo Ezekiel's valley of dry bones, where the Spirit raises a dead Israel to life — a paradigm of resurrection-as-restoration. Thematically coherent with Paul's resurrection horizon; verbally faint, marked contested.

echoes.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters. God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
echoes.note: 'Calls the things that are not, as though they were' (4:17) figurally echoes the creation account, where God's word summons being out of nonbeing ('Let there be... and there was').
